hussars: light cavalry soldiers, typically mounted troops in the army
gendarme: French rural police officer, a member of the armed police
gendarmes: members of the French armed police force in the countryside
commandant: army officer in charge of a garrison or fortified town
detachment: small group of soldiers sent away from the main force
militia: part-time citizen soldiers, not members of the regular army
vent-hole: small opening in a cannon through which the charge was fired
litter: stretcher used to carry the wounded or sick
chateau: French country mansion or castle, often a noble family's home
cubic: relating to volume measured in three dimensions, such as a cubic metre
leagues: old units of distance, roughly three miles each
paces: steps taken while walking, used as a measure of distance
councillor: elected member of a town or village council
magistrate: local judge who hears minor legal cases
usher: attendant who shows people to their seats or places
baron: nobleman holding a lower rank of hereditary title
countess: noblewoman holding the title of a count or earl
proprietor: owner of a property, shop, or business
hedges: rows of bushes or shrubs marking the edges of fields
cider: alcoholic drink made from fermented apple juice
dumplings: balls of boiled dough, cooked in soup or stew
coach: horse-drawn carriage for carrying passengers over long distances
fetch: go somewhere and bring back a person or object
mademoiselle: French form of address for an unmarried woman or young lady
oiseau: French word meaning bird, used here as a name or nickname
cavalier: horseman or soldier on horseback, or a courteous gentleman
ardent: passionate, eager, or full of intense feeling
hlans: Prussian lancer cavalry soldiers, armed with long spears
wretch: miserable or unfortunate person, often one deserving pity
stupefied: dazed and unable to think clearly, stunned by shock
impassive: showing no emotion or reaction, calm and unmoved
melancholy: deep, quiet sadness, often mixed with thoughtful reflection
indistinct: unclear or hard to see, hear, or make out
gasping: breathing in short, sharp, difficult gulps, often from shock
bewildered: confused and unable to understand what is happening
sobbing: crying with short, broken, noisy breaths
stout: rather fat, or sturdy and strong in build
vanquished: defeated in battle or in a contest
conquerors: those who have won a war and taken control of territory
gallantry: polite, respectful courtesy shown especially toward women
obliging: willing and ready to help or do favours for others
sentiment: feeling or emotion, especially a tender or sentimental one
relic: old object kept because of its link to the past
gallop: fast running pace of a horse, faster than a trot
rumbling: low, heavy, continuous sound, like distant thunder or wheels
shrill: high-pitched, sharp, and piercing in sound
uttered: spoke or made a sound aloud, often briefly or with effort
hesitate: pause before acting or speaking because of doubt
cannon: heavy mounted gun that fires large projectiles in war
tremble: shake slightly from fear, cold, or strong emotion
sabre: curved cavalry sword with a single sharp edge
hussar: light cavalry soldier in the army, known for fast horsemanship
wrinkled: creased or folded into lines, especially on skin or cloth
